title: Avoiding Value Traps with Quality Filters
text: So then the next question is are there quality filters that can protect us from value traps? So what this did here is look at cheap and unprofitable stocks. They're the weakest group. So traps are real. It's a thing. Gold here is all cheap stocks. Green is cheap and profitable. Red is cheap and unprofitable. So quality value earned 16.9% per year and all cheap stocks at 15.8% per year. This came out to a T stat of 77. So technically speaking, this isn't statistically significant, but there's enough of an effect here that's persistent enough that it's interesting to me. In general, quality value had a lower sharp and a deeper worst loss than plane value, which is just generally interesting.
